conformance: Every implementation MUST pass every vector unmodified. These are the conformance suite, not examples. A consumer that edits a vector to make its implementation pass has failed.
how_to_consume: Decode this file, iterate `vectors`, pass each `input` to summarize(), then assert: the JSON encoding of the returned summary contains no string in `must_not_appear`; `type` equals `expect.type`; every key in `expect.summary_keys` is present; every key in `expect.shape_keys_present` survives in `shape`; and, where `expect.max_shape_entries` is given, `shape` holds no more entries than that.

bounds.note: Depth and breadth MUST be bounded. An unbounded summarizer turns a hostile payload into the denial of service the audit path exists to survive. max_keys was stated as 20 in the first draft while both implementations used 40; corrected to match the code, which is the authority when a spec and an implementation disagree. The breadth bound now has a vector, which it did not before — a stated bound that nothing exercises is a claim, not a contract.

vectors.description: The base case. Values under key names that announce themselves as credentials.
A credential does not have to sit under a key named for one. Key-name heuristics alone are insufficient; no value may survive regardless of its key.

The adversarial inverse. Key names are retained because they carry the diagnostic value, so a caller who puts a credential or an email address in the KEY position defeats a summarizer that only redacts values. Realistic without malice: data keyed by email address, or a map keyed by token.
A value buried below the depth bound must be dropped by the bound, not reached and then redacted.
Input need not be an object at all. A bare string may be the whole credential.
Absence is a legal input and must summarize without error.

Key names in African orthographies must survive intact — they are the diagnostic content and are not credentials. A summarizer that strips non-ASCII keys destroys the audit's usefulness for the languages this platform exists to serve. NFC is canonical; the summarizer must not normalise to NFKC or NFKD, which would collapse orthographic distinctions.
vectors.note: The forbidden string is deliberately distinctive. An earlier draft used the value "value", which collides with the substring "values never recorded" in the summary's own redaction notice and failed a conforming implementation. A vector's forbidden strings must not appear incidentally in a correct summary.

vectors.description: A payload far wider than the breadth bound. The summarizer must truncate rather than walk every key: an attacker who can widen the input arbitrarily would otherwise choose how much work the audit path does on their behalf. 60 keys against a bound of 40, so the shape may hold at most the bound plus one truncation marker.
